audits.title: A multi-district audit against national guidelines for the management of uncomplicated genital Chlamydia trachomatis infection.
audits.standard: National guidelines for management of uncomplicated genital chlamydial infection (selected standards)
audits.setting: Nine genitourinary medicine clinics, Yorkshire region

cycle1.result: Variations in compliance with confirmation of test results and time from diagnosis to treatment; recording of discussions, advice and contact tracing limited or separate from the main record.

audits.other_findings: Multi-district audit using peripatetic audit workers; re-audit with the same standards was committed to.
audits.citation: Clarke J, Preston AD. A multi-district audit against national guidelines for the management of uncomplicated genital Chlamydia trachomatis infection. Int J STD AIDS. 2001;12(10):677-686. doi:10.1258/0956462011923912. PMID: 11564336.

audits.title: Treatment of Chlamydia trachomatis in North Thames region 2003.
audits.standard: National guidelines for antibiotic treatment of chlamydia and test of cure
audits.setting: Multicentre GU clinics, North Thames region

cycle2.result: Significant increase in centres following national antibiotic prescribing guidelines and offering test of cure when indicated.

audits.citation: Sethi G, Forster GE, Brook MG, Jones K, Daniels D, Horner PJ, et al.. Treatment of Chlamydia trachomatis in North Thames region 2003. Int J STD AIDS. 2004;15(12):831-832. doi:10.1258/0956462042563657. PMID: 15643698.

audits.title: An audit of the interval to treatment of anogenital Chlamydia trachomatis at Scottish genitourinary medicine clinics.
audits.standard: National standard and local best practice target for interval to chlamydia treatment

cycle1.result: Three clinics treated 95% within two weeks and 10 clinics treated 95% within four weeks; all clinics treated 60% within four weeks.

audits.other_findings: Clinics performed well against published standards but less well against the best practice target.
audits.citation: Steedman N, Oroz C, Fernando I, Baguley S. An audit of the interval to treatment of anogenital Chlamydia trachomatis at Scottish genitourinary medicine clinics. Int J STD AIDS. 2008;19(2):121-122. doi:10.1258/ijsa.2007.007154. PMID: 18334067.

audits.title: UK National Audit of chlamydial infection management in sexual health clinics. case notes audit: demography, diagnosis and treatment.
audits.standard: UK National Guideline for chlamydial infection
audits.setting: 193 UK sexual health clinics (national web-based audit)

cycle1.result: 93% of cases had genital NAATs; azithromycin used more than doxycycline (54% vs 37%); 93% of women with genital NAATs sampled from cervix or vulvovaginal area.

audits.other_findings: 20 of 26 pregnant women treated with azithromycin; about half of cases had no symptoms.
audits.citation: McClean H, Carne C, Bunting P, Bhaduri S, Fernandes A, Dhar J, et al.. UK National Audit of chlamydial infection management in sexual health clinics. case notes audit: demography, diagnosis and treatment. Int J STD AIDS. 2008;19(7):469-472. doi:10.1258/ijsa.2008.008137. PMID: 18574119.

audits.title: A multi-setting audit of the management of genital Chlamydia trachomatis infection.
audits.standard: 2008 Ministry of Health chlamydia management guidelines
audits.setting: 19 settings diagnosing chlamydia, Waikato District Health Board

cycle1.result: Treatment documented in 380 (91.6%); 369 (97.1%) of these treated within 28 days (88.9% of all cases); effective partner notification lacking.

audits.other_findings: Documentation of discussions and outcomes was limited; re-audit committed to.
audits.citation: Morgan J, Donnell A, Bell A. A multi-setting audit of the management of genital Chlamydia trachomatis infection. N Z Med J. 2010;123(1315):42-54. PMID: 20581930.

audits.title: How accurate is presumptive Chlamydia trachomatis treatment? A 6-month clinical audit of a walk-in sexual health service.
audits.standard: STI guidelines recommending presumptive chlamydia treatment when symptomatic

cycle1.result: 54% negative for all pathogens; 25% positive for chlamydia; 20% negative for chlamydia but positive for another pathogen.

audits.other_findings: Presumptive treatment resulted in over-treatment; audit fed back to the service.
audits.citation: Jacups SP, Potter C, Yarwood T, Doyle-Adams S, Russell D. How accurate is presumptive Chlamydia trachomatis treatment? A 6-month clinical audit of a walk-in sexual health service. Sex Health. 2021;18(5):413-420. doi:10.1071/sh21078. PMID: 34742364.
